content.title: Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov fight date, time, where to watch
content.text: April 11, 2026, 9:00 a.m. MTTyson Fury returns from a .year-long retirement that followed his only two losses when he steps into the ring against Arslanbek Makhmudov in London.Fury, who at one point unified the heavyweight titles a decade ago, retired in January 2025 after consecutive losses to Oleksandr Usyk, but ended that retirement for this bout against the Russian Makhmudov.Maknudov has won his last two fights, but Fury is a substantial favorite in what amounts to a home bout for the Englishman.How to watch Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov fightTyson Fury's comeback fight against Arslanbek Makhmudov airs live on Netflix, free to subscribers.How to watch: NetflixTyson Fury next fight: Fight date, timeCoverage of the Fury vs. Makhmudov fight card starts on Netflix at noon MT/1 p.m. CT on Saturday, April 11. Ring walks for the main event are at approximately 3 p.m. MT/4 p.m. CT.Fight card start: noon MT/1 p.m. CTFury vs. Makhmudov ring walks: approx. 3 p.m. MT/4 p.m. CTTyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov undercardThe undercard to Fury vs. Makhmudov features 24-1 Conor Benn against 30-3 Regis Prograis.Tyson Fury (34-2-1, 24 KOs) vs. Arslanbek Makhmudov (21-2, 19 KOs) heavyweightConor Benn (24-1, 14 KOs) vs. Regis Prograis (30-3, 24 KOs) supermiddleweightRichard Riakporhe (19-1, 15 KOs) vs. Jeamie Tshikeva (9-2, 5 KOs) flyweightFrazer Clarke (9-2-1, 7 KOs) vs. Justis Huni (12-1, 7 KOs) middleweightTyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov fight locationThe Tyson Fury vs. Arslanbek Makhmudov fight card will be held at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in north London. Fury fought Derek Chisora in the same venue in 2022.Location: Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London, UKTyson Fury recordTyson Fury is 34-2-1 with 24 wins by knockout.The Manchester-born Fury unified the heavyweight titles in 2015-16 and was the WBC title holder from 2020-24.Tyson Fury weight, heightThe 37-year-old Fury is 6-foot-9 with an 85-inch reach. Fury has been a heavyweight his entire career and weighed an average of 273.5 pounds across his last three bouts.Where is Tyson Fury fromTyson Fury was born and fights out of Manchester, England, UK.Arslanbek Makhmudov recordArslanbek Makhmudov is 21-2 with 19 wins by knockout.Makhmudov most recently defeated David Allen by unanimous decision in October. His two defeats were in 2023 and 2024 to Agit Kabayel and Guido Vianello.Arslanbek Makhmudov weight, heightThe 36-year-old Arslanbek Makhmudov is 6-foot-5½ with a 72-inch reach. Makhmudov has been a heavyweight his entire career and weighed an average of 262 pounds across his last three bouts.Where is Arslanbek Makhmudov fromMakhumudov is from Mozdok, Russia and fights out of Montreal, Quebec, Canada.Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov oddsOdds from BetMGM.com: Fury -500, Makhmudov +333Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov predictions, picksBad Left Hook: Fury by 8th round TKOPatrick Stumberg writes: "If he can’t outmaneuver or outlast Fury, that leaves an early finish as Makhmudov’s best chance of victory. Unfortunately, if there’s one thing we know about “The Gypsy King,” it’s that he doesn’t go away easy. It wouldn’t be shocking to see Makhmudov clip him with a stray shot, but keeping him down seems beyond his capabilities."We’ve seen Makhmudov’s ceiling and it’s below Fury’s floor. Fury drains his gas tank and pours it on for a finish before the championship rounds."Odds shark: Take Maknudov with the oddsEthan Diamandas writes: "The value here sits with the underdog. Makhmudov at +400 offers significant upside against a fighter who looked diminished in his last two outings and hasn't competed in over a year."While Fury remains the superior boxer technically, Father Time and ring rust don't respect pedigree. No sir. Makhmudov's power and pressure style poses a legitimate knockout threat, especially if Fury's reflexes have slowed during his time away. Don't dump your whole bankroll into this dude, but keep Makhmudov in mind as an underdog when the time comes."Free Super Tips: Fury to win in rounds 7-12Gareth Freeman writes: "Makhmudov has a 21-2 record and is coming into this contest on the back of a points win over Dave Allen. His two losses have come via stoppages, to Agit Kabayel and Guido Vianello, and Fury should be able to force a stoppage here even if he isn’t a huge puncher himself."The Russian is lacking in defensive skills and can be an easy target. Fury doesn’t have the kind of power that will allow him to just blow the 36-year-old away in one visit but he should be able to pick Makhmudov off as the rounds progress and he can force a stoppage in the second half of the fight."Heavyweightboxing.com: Fury by decision"over the course of the fight, Fury’s superior boxing ability, experience, and adaptability are expected to separate him from a more one-dimensional opponent. Once Fury finds his rhythm, he should be able to manage distance, pick his shots more cleanly, and gradually take control of the contest."Bret Bloomquist can be reached at bbloomquist@elpasotimes.com; @Bretbloomquist on X.
